主要内容: On March 6, 2019, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) announced that Russian telecommunications provider Mobile TeleSystems PJSC (MTS) will pay $100 million to resolve charges of violating the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA). The SEC alleged that MTS bribed an Uzbek official connected to the former President of Uzbekistan, enabling the company to secure business in the country. During the scheme, MTS made at least $420 million in illicit payments, which allowed it to operate in Uzbekistan’s telecommunications market for eight years, generating over $2.4 billion in revenue. In 2012, the Uzbek government expropriated MTS’s operations. The bribes were disguised as acquisition costs, option payments, and charitable donations. MTS consented to the SEC’s order, which found violations of the anti-bribery, books and records, and internal accounting control provisions of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. In a related matter, MTS entered into a deferred prosecution agreement with the U.S. Department of Justice and agreed to pay a criminal fine of $850 million. The SEC and U.S. authorities recovered $2.6 billion through these actions.
